_meta.purpose: Grounding data for Riftbound + multi-game registry design work. Every value below was read from real files in the MetaSurf main repo (branch multi-tcg-wave1) on 2026-07-09. Nothing is invented.

IMAGE_POLICY_CRITICAL.riftbound: DO NOT HOTLINK RIFTBOUND CARD IMAGES. The Riftcodex catalogue's media.image_url points at Riot's CDN (cmsassets.rgpub.io). Per the owner's ToS decision (2026-07-08, unregistered posture vs Riot's metagame-data ban): no Riot API, no CDN hotlinks. The catalogue adapter deliberately does NOT carry image URLs into card attrs. Riftbound card slots must render as domain-colored placeholder frames with the card name.
IMAGE_POLICY_CRITICAL.onepiece: Only use image URLs found in local grounding data; none are included in this file, so use color-framed placeholders.
IMAGE_POLICY_CRITICAL.mtg: Scryfall image URLs from grounding data are fine to hotlink (none included in this file).

contract_GameUiConfig.pipPalette: Record<string, {bg, fg}> keyed by the game's own colour codes (cards.attrs color_identity vocabulary)
contract_GameUiConfig.pipOrder: display order of pip codes; codes not listed sort first (legacy indexOf semantics)
contract_GameUiConfig.colorlessCode: code rendered when a deck/card has no colours
contract_GameUiConfig.typeGroupOrder: type-group match + display order for the deck view; matched by substring against the front face of the card's type_line, first hit wins; 'Other' is the catch-all and must be last

game_ui_registry.lookup: gameUi(game?: string) — route slugs are /{game}/{format}/...; unknown/missing slugs fall back to mtg

onepiece.notes: Codes are the punk-records catalogue's own vocabulary; multicolour cards carry two codes and render two pips; no colourless One Piece card observed — '—' is defensive fallback only. Leader is the archetype axis.

riftbound.notes: Domain codes are the game's own color_identity vocabulary as observed in the real Riftcodex capture. The swatch hues are the PROJECT'S provisional design choices — no official palette was ingested (Riot assets off-limits). pipOrder is alphabetical pending any data-backed canonical order. Legend first in typeGroupOrder because it defines the deck (archetype_axis).

registry_seam_gaps: ColorPips renders the raw code text inside the pip, so Riftbound pips show full domain words ('Body', 'Chaos') and One Piece pips show full colour words — a per-code short-label extension to GameUiConfig is a flagged gap (owner call), not yet implemented.

No display-name metadata (e.g. 'Riftbound' vs slug 'riftbound') exists in the registry; slugs are the only client-side identity. Format display metadata comes from GET /v1/games config passthrough instead.

riftbound_catalogue.source: Riftcodex community API capture 2026-07-08 (api.riftcodex.com — NOT the Riot API; keyless; robots.txt has no Disallow). Raw archive: 11 pages x 100, total 1,064 printings, verified against docs/notes/riftcodex-observed-schema.md.
riftbound_catalogue.granularity: printing-level (unlike the oracle-level MTG catalogue); 979 distinct playable names over 1,059 playable items; 24-hex 'id' is the unique canonical_ref; riftbound_id is NOT unique (16 OPP base/(Metal) pairs share one).
domain_facts: classification.domain is a list, length 1 (873 cards) or 2 (191 cards).
Every Legend has exactly 2 domains (0 exceptions in corpus).
Battlefields are always ['Colorless'] (all 57; also the only landscape-orientation cards).
Runes carry exactly 1 real domain; the 6 base runes are one per domain.
'Colorless' is the source's explicit none-marker (62 cards: 57 Battlefields + 5 Tokens); stored as [] in attrs, rendered via colorlessCode.

deck_shape.source: config/formats.json, game 'riftbound', format 'constructed' — VERIFIED, matches the 'legend + 40 main + 12 runes + 3 battlefields' brief
deck_shape.note: main is min 40 with NO max in config (i.e. 40+, not exactly 40).

units_sample.name: Vilemaw
units_sample.note: base printing exists; alt-art row shown in fixture

riftbound_catalogue.attribute_semantics: attributes {energy, might, power} always present, ints or null. Legends/Battlefields/Runes: all-null. Units: energy+might (power on some). Spells/Gear: energy (power on some). Energy range observed 0-12.

api_shapes.source: api/routes.py + api/schemas.py (branch multi-tcg-wave1), field lists copied verbatim from the pydantic models

formats.name: str (format slug)
formats.config: dict — the format's config/formats.json entry passed through VERBATIM from seeded formats.config (zone maps, zone_sizes, archetype_axis, board_zones, etc.). Clients enumerate this instead of baking in what exists.

POST /v1/{game}/{format}/classify.auth: premium (403 without entitlement); 501 if no ClassifierService registered for the game
POST /v1/{game}/{format}/classify.classifier_registration_fact: serve.py registers classifiers={'mtg': MtgClassifierService()} ONLY — onepiece and riftbound classify currently returns 501 'classification not available for this game'

request_ClassifyRequest.cards: list[ClassifyCard], 1..500 items; ClassifyCard = { name: str (min 1 char), count: int (1..250), board: str }

response_ClassifyResponse.archetype_id: int | null (null when the archetype has no stored decks yet)
response_ClassifyResponse.name: str (archetype name)
response_ClassifyResponse.unresolved_cards: list[str] — names that did not resolve to known cards; reported, never guessed
response_ClassifyResponse.matchup_spread: list[SpreadCell] = { archetype_id, name, p_win, ci_lo, ci_hi, n_matches }

query.as_of: date, optional; default latest rollup_emerging snapshot

EmergingCluster.cluster_key: int — local, within-snapshot handle; NOT a stable archetype id
EmergingCluster.named: bool — ALWAYS false in this feed; explicit so clients render 'unnamed / emerging'
EmergingCluster.provisional_descriptor: str — colour group + top signature card, flagged 'Unnamed:' — never a curated archetype name
EmergingCluster.color: str — WUBRG identity string ('' -> colorless). NOTE: schema comment is MTG-vocabulary; game-neutral value is the game's colour codes
EmergingCluster.recent_decks: int — decks seen in the most recent 7 days of the window (the growth signal)
EmergingCluster.winrate: float | null — cluster winrate over decided stored games; null when no match data

SignatureCard.name: str
SignatureCard.in_cluster_freq: float — fraction of the cluster's decks playing the card
SignatureCard.out_cluster_freq: float — fraction of out-of-cluster decks playing it
SignatureCard.lift: float — in_cluster_freq / max(out_cluster_freq, floor) — the signal

attribution.where: EventsResponse.credits — clients must display required credits visibly with link

gaps_and_honest_limits: NO Riftbound decklists, events, archetypes, or winrates exist anywhere in the repo — formats.json has riftbound constructed with import:false, and no Riftbound event source is ingested. Any Riftbound meta/matchup/emerging numbers in a mockup are PLACEHOLDER and must be labeled as such.
NO official Riftbound domain colour palette was ingested; the riftbound.ts hues are the project's provisional design choices, and pipOrder is alphabetical pending a data-backed canonical order.
The Riftcodex API has NO legality field — rotation/ban legality cannot be shown for Riftbound (recorded owner blocker).
Riftcodex data carries no stated license (recorded owner blocker).
No GameUiConfig short-label support: pips render full domain words for Riftbound / colour words for One Piece (flagged registry seam gap).
The classify endpoint is registered for mtg only (serve.py); riftbound/onepiece classify returns 501 today.
EmergingCluster.color is documented in schemas.py as a WUBRG string — the emerging feed has only ever run on MTG data; no Riftbound emerging rows exist.
Riftbound main deck is min 40 with no configured max (not 'exactly 40'); legend exactly 1, runes exactly 12, battlefields exactly 3 (config/formats.json).

The riftbound_catalogue samples above are printings from the raw capture; the full base catalogue has 754 base non-promo playable printings — use only names listed here (or re-mine the capture) in design work.
